expected_effect: No action taken, so nothing changes. A restart would only be verifiable if a post-restart mongod startup in Loki were NOT followed within ~10s by a SignalHandler shutdown - but we never saw whether mongodb-rate recovered after 15:01:10 (log window ends 15:02:30), and no metrics exist for this service, so the effect is currently unobservable.
if_wrong: If a Loki query past 15:02:30 shows mongodb-rate still absent or looping startup/SIGTERM, and a kubelet/pod-event check shows no external killer still active, then restart_service becomes justified and this abstention was too cautious. Conversely, if pod events name the fault-injection ConfigMap as the killer, a restart would be re-killed and the fix lies outside this system.
risk: Abstaining leaves the rate datastore down if it never came back, so hotel-reservation callers keep failing. Restarting instead would risk recreating a container that the still-active external killer terminates again, masking the real cause and burning the one-shot (irreversible) restart while confidence is low.
blast_radius: No one sees a change now. Any later restart touches mongodb-rate only, with callers in the hotel-reservation namespace (the rate service) seeing connection resets during recreate.
